content: 1. Calcium carbonate reduces the levels of beta-blocker betaxolol by inhibiting its gastrointestinal (GI) absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. It is recommended to use caution, monitor closely, and separate administration by at least 2 hours. 2. Magnesium hydroxide decreases the levels or effects of bictegravir through cation binding in the GI tract. Therapy should be modified or monitored closely. Bictegravir can be taken on an empty stomach at least 2 hours before antacids containing aluminum, magnesium, or calcium. However, bictegravir and calcium-containing supplements can be taken together with food. Routine administration of bictegravir under fasting conditions simultaneously with, or 2 hours after, calcium supplements or antacids containing calcium is not recommended. 3. Calcium carbonate reduces the effects of bisoprolol by an unspecified mechanism and decreases its levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution, monitor closely, and separate administration by at least 2 hours. 4. Blessed thistle reduces the effects of famotidine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Similarly, blessed thistle reduces the effects of calcium carbonate through pharmacodynamic antagonism, with unknown clinical significance. 5. Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of bosutinib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Famotidine also decreases the levels or effects of bosutinib by increasing gastric pH. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 6. Calcium carbonate reduces the effects of budesonide by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is advised. Additionally, the dissolution of extended-release budesonide tablets is pH-dependent. Famotidine similarly decreases the effects of budesonide by increasing gastric pH. 7. Budesonide decreases the levels of calcium carbonate by increasing its elimination. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 8. Bumetanide decreases the levels of magnesium hydroxide and calcium carbonate by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of these interactions is unknown. 9. Magnesium hydroxide reduces the levels or effects of cabotegravir through cation binding in the GI tract. Therapy should be modified or monitored closely. Calcium carbonate similarly decreases the levels or effects of cabotegravir through cation binding. Antacid products should be administered at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after taking oral cabotegravir. 10. Caffeine decreases the levels of calcium carbonate by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 11. Calcitonin salmon increases the levels of magnesium hydroxide by decreasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 12. Topical calcitriol increases the levels of calcium carbonate through pharmacodynamic synergism, potentially leading to hypercalcemia. Close monitoring is recommended. 13. Calcium carbonate reduces the effects of captopril by an unspecified mechanism and may decrease its absorption. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Famotidine decreases the levels or effects of carbonyl iron by increasing gastric pH. Calcium carbonate similarly decreases the levels or effects of carbonyl iron by increasing gastric pH. These interactions apply only to the oral forms of both agents. Carbonyl iron increases the levels of calcium carbonate by enhancing GI absorption. 15. Calcium carbonate reduces the levels of carvedilol by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution, monitor closely, and separate administration by at least 2 hours. 16. Famotidine decreases the levels or effects of cefdinir by increasing gastric pH. Calcium carbonate similarly decreases the levels or effects of cefdinir by increasing gastric pH. These interactions apply only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Famotidine decreases the levels or effects of cefditoren by increasing gastric pH. Calcium carbonate similarly decreases the levels or effects of cefditoren by increasing gastric pH. These interactions apply only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Famotidine decreases the levels or effects of cefpodoxime by increasing gastric pH. Calcium carbonate similarly decreases the levels or effects of cefpodoxime by increasing gastric pH. These interactions apply only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Famotidine decreases the levels or effects of ceftibuten by increasing gastric pH. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 20. The combination of calcium carbonate and intravenous ceftriaxone is contraindicated due to the risk of potentially fatal particulate precipitation in the lungs and kidneys. Calcium-containing solutions, including Ringer or Hartmann solutions, should not be used with IV ceftriaxone. Separate administration by at least 48 hours.
